headline: Multi-omic and genetic integration nominates causal targets in aging and disease
label: Multiomics Causal Target Discovery
summary: Large multiomic cohorts, single-nucleus atlases, and trial-embedded aging clocks now let teams test whether molecular readouts reflect causal mechanisms.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the combination of genetic association, multilayer omics, and aging or disease readouts to move from correlative molecular signatures toward candidate causal targets. FM-GPT applies Bayesian fine mapping to prioritize causal genes across correlated phenotypes in phenome-wide TWAS, and a single-nucleus atlas of over 3 million nuclei from 791 Alzheimer's disease individuals resolves cell-type-specific programs through the MONET framework. Multi-omic studies of cognitive resilience and multilevel genomic, transcriptomic, and epidemiologic evidence linking diabetic retinopathy to Alzheimer disease extend this integration to disease comparison, while a longitudinal gene expression and metabolomics study of an aging population cohort characterizes spatiotemporal dynamics. What is newer is the use of proteomic aging clocks as readouts in a phase 2a trial, assessing geroprotective effects alongside conventional outcomes. Not all items share this design; the SIRT6 transcriptomic biomarker evaluation and the transformer-based ischemic stroke risk model are more descriptive or predictive.
